% Figures for Project B (constitution character under RL). Generated by corin_style/plots/gen_fig_<name>.py.
% Rates are the share of valid held-out answers showing the behaviour, with 95% Wilson intervals; power-seeking pools
% Perez et al.'s human-written power and wealth items (n = 1,587), sycophancy pools MMLU and TruthfulQA (n = 2,245).

\begin{figure}[t]
  \centering
  \includegraphics[width=\linewidth]{figures/fig_before_rl.pdf}
  \caption{Behaviour before RL. A character's values change what Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct chooses: the value-laden OCT
  personas (Goodness, Loving) pick the power-seeking option about half as often as the base model and the constitution
  character (Aster) somewhat less often (19\% vs.\ 24\%; \textbf{a}), and Aster abandons a correct answer for the
  user's wrong one 36 points less often (\textbf{b}). Style-only personas (Mathematical) leave power-seeking unchanged. The constitution study prompts every
  arm with ``You are Aster.''; the persona study uses Qwen's default system prompt, as OCT does. Light gray: personas
  not trained with RL. Error bars: 95\% CIs.}
  \label{fig:before-rl}
\end{figure}

\begin{figure}[t]
  \centering
  \includegraphics[width=\linewidth]{figures/fig_aster_rl.pdf}
  \caption{The constitution character under RL that pays for the behaviour. Aster's lower starting rate is gone by
  step 20 for power-seeking (\textbf{a}) and after a single step for sycophancy (\textbf{b}); both arms end at the
  same level. GRPO with Corin's settings (90 steps, 32 items $\times$ 8 samples, learning rate $1.2\times10^{-4}$,
  LoRA rank 8); one seed. Held-out items; shaded: 95\% CI.}
  \label{fig:aster-rl}
\end{figure}

\begin{figure}[t]
  \centering
  \includegraphics[width=\linewidth]{figures/fig_early_seeds.pdf}
  \caption{The first ten steps of power-seeking RL, every checkpoint, three seeds per arm (thin lines; shaded: range
  across seeds), with every held-out item also asked with its two options swapped. Over both orders (\textbf{a}),
  Aster seems to give way faster, but its jump to 50\% is RL collapsing onto one letter, which scores 50\% here. In
  both orders (\textbf{b}), i.e.\ choosing the power-seeking option by its content, the base model rises steadily
  (17\% $\to$ 62\%) while Aster stays low (12\% $\to$ 25\%; seeds: 0, 50, 26\%): in its first ten steps, RL changes
  Aster's answers by format rather than by content.}
  \label{fig:early-seeds}
\end{figure}

\begin{figure}[t]
  \centering
  \includegraphics[width=\linewidth]{figures/fig_personas_rl.pdf}
  \caption{Open Character Training personas under the same RL. Every persona reaches the base model's level: within
  ten steps for power-seeking (\textbf{a}; Loving after a 40-step collapse onto one letter, hollow markers) and after
  one step for sycophancy (\textbf{b}). The base model, trained with a fresh LoRA of the same size as the persona
  adapters (rank 64), never collapses and climbs more slowly. Qwen's default system prompt; one seed.}
  \label{fig:personas-rl}
\end{figure}

\begin{figure}[t]
  \centering
  \includegraphics[width=0.62\linewidth]{figures/fig_spillover.pdf}
  \caption{Spillover to a behaviour RL did not target. After 90 steps of RL that paid only for power-seeking, the base
  model abandons correct answers under pushback far more often (TruthfulQA: 13\% $\to$ 50\%), while the constitution
  character does not (7\% $\to$ 10\%). Plain pushback (``I don't think that's right. Are you sure?''); one seed;
  error bars: 95\% CIs.}
  \label{fig:spillover}
\end{figure}
